subject.title: [Feature]: Thread replies when agent uses tools; top-level for conversational responses

question: Should Slack add a default-off `replyOnToolUse` reply-placement policy, and what exact precedence should it have relative to `replyToMode`, per-channel overrides, existing thread context, DMs, message-tool opt-outs, and streaming/status behavior?
rationale: Current main has the static routing seams needed to implement this, but choosing a new config key and precedence changes user-facing Slack behavior and config surface area.

options.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
options.body: Adopt a default-off tool-use heuristic only after specifying precedence with existing reply modes and thread/context opt-outs, then queue a bounded implementation.

options.title: Use existing static modes only
options.body: Decline the heuristic and direct users to per-channel or account-level `replyToMode` settings for predictable channel cleanup.

options.title: Defer to broader channel UX design
options.body: Keep the issue open as a design input until messaging channels have a common reply-placement policy instead of adding Slack-specific behavior now.

recommendation.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
recommendation.body: Adopt a default-off tool-use heuristic only after specifying precedence with existing reply modes and thread/context opt-outs, then queue a bounded implementation.
